content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone of the head, above and between the eyes: smooth, glossy dark cuticle, one horn curving upward and back from the head; long curved head horn. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and rows of small breathing openings (spiracles) along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing hybrid creature concept**
I'm planning a single creature with a brown bear silhouette and fur, adding a smooth glossy beetle horn curving up from the frontal bone above the eyes, keeping the head clear and uncluttered.
**Reviewing beetle reference details**
I'm checking reference details for the European rhinoceros beetle to confirm horn shape, body proportions, and texture before finalizing the illustration.
**Generating hybrid creature image**
I'm creating the hybrid image with four legs and brown bear paws with claws, building on the beetle reference details to finalize the creature concept.
**Drafting hybrid illustration prompt**
I'm shaping the prompt for a natural-history illustration of a brown bear with a glossy dark horn and rows of spiracles along the flanks, using a side three-quarter view on a plain light background.
**Refining hybrid creature design**
I'm adjusting the prompt to reduce the armor and better integrate the spiracles along the flanks with arthropod features, then generating another version for the user.
